title: Do I Need an ISBN to Self-Publish? Free vs Paid ISBNs Explained | Legenddary's SparkPrep
h1: Do you need an ISBN to self-publish? Free vs paid, in plain English
description: What an ISBN is, when you need one, what it costs ($125 for one from Bowker, or free from KDP and IngramSpark), and the catch with free ISBNs. Written for first-time authors.
lead: An ISBN is the 13-digit number that identifies your book. New authors often think they must buy one before anything else. You might not need to. Here is the simple version.

answer.q: Do I need an ISBN to self-publish a book?
answer.a: For a print book, yes, but it can be free. Amazon KDP and IngramSpark (U.S. authors) both give free ISBNs. A KDP ebook needs no ISBN at all. Buy your own from Bowker ($125 for one, $295 for ten) only if you want your own publisher name on the book and full control.

body:
What an ISBN is

ISBN stands for International Standard Book Number. It is a 13-digit number that tells stores and libraries exactly which book, which edition and which format they are ordering. It is usually printed above the barcode on your back cover.

  • Each format needs its own ISBN: paperback, hardcover and ebook are three different numbers.
  • An ISBN does not give you copyright. You own your writing either way.
  • ISBNs never expire, so you can buy some now and use them later.

Your three choices

CostPublisher name on the bookCan you use it elsewhere?
Free KDP ISBN (paperback/hardcover)$0"Independently published"No, Amazon only
Free IngramSpark ISBN (U.S. only)$0IngramSpark's imprint, not yoursNo, it stays with IngramSpark
Your own ISBN from Bowker (U.S.)$125 for 1, $295 for 10, $575 for 100Your name or your imprintYes, anywhere

Prices from Bowker's myidentifiers.com and IngramSpark's own help pages, checked November 2026. Bowker is the official ISBN agency for the United States; other countries have their own (Canada gives them out free).

What about ebooks?

A Kindle ebook on KDP does not need an ISBN. Amazon gives it its own number, called an ASIN. Other ebook stores and IngramSpark ask for one, and it must be different from your print ISBN.

So which should a first-time author pick?

  • Just testing the waters on Amazon? The free KDP ISBN is fine.
  • Want bookstores and libraries too? Buying 10 ISBNs ($295) is the most common choice. It covers a paperback, hardcover and ebook, with numbers left over for your next book, and you can use the same number on KDP and IngramSpark.
  • Building a brand or a series? Own your ISBNs, so your publisher name is the same on every book.

The mistake that gets books rejected

The ISBN in your book details must match the barcode on your cover and the number on your copyright page. A mismatch is one of the most common reasons a file is sent back. SparkPrep, an Automated Publishing Production System (A.P.P.S.), reads the barcode on your cover and checks it against the ISBN you entered before you upload. Read more: how to fix an ISBN mismatch and where the barcode goes.

faq.q: How much does an ISBN cost?
faq.a: In the U.S., Bowker charges $125 for one ISBN, $295 for ten and $575 for one hundred. KDP and IngramSpark (for U.S. authors) also offer free ISBNs, but they can only be used with that company.

faq.q: Can I use the same ISBN for my paperback and ebook?
faq.a: No. Every format needs its own ISBN. A paperback, a hardcover and an ebook are three different numbers.

faq.q: Can I use a free KDP ISBN on IngramSpark?
faq.a: No. A free KDP ISBN can only be used on Amazon. To sell the same paperback through IngramSpark, use your own ISBN on both.
